title: Slimchain castless in-place kernel scheduler for streaming attention
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Streaming attention paths currently allocate small transient tensors and perform explicit dequant/cast copies when switching between INT8/FP8 and FP32 execution. For short prefill windows and low-latency decode, the allocation + copy tax dominates the token latency for many workloads (observed at 95th percentile on small-context requests).

Goal: Implement an in-place, castless execution path and a lightweight scheduler (Slimchain) that keeps quantized buffers reusable across prefill->decode boundary and prefers kernels that accept packed INT8/FP8 layouts. This reduces allocation churn and eliminates an extra memory pass for common streaming patterns, improving P95 decode latency and lowering GPU memory traffic without changing model semantics or accuracy.%
acceptance_criteria: New Slimchain scheduler selects castless kernels for headwise-attention when buffer layout matches and the request latency SLO is active
End-to-end P95 token latency improvement >= 8% on streaming small-context benchmark suite (internal perfset/stream-7k)
No regressions (>0.5% token-level perplexity change) on existing eval prompts compared to baseline FP32 path
Fallback: correct and measurable fallback to existing dequantized kernels when buffer misalignment or mixed-precision constraints are detected
Unit and integration tests cover allocator behavior, kernel selection rules, and a simulated prefill->decode handoff
technical_notes:
Design summary: introduce a slim metadata tag on GPU buffers indicating: format (INT8/FP8/FP32), layout (packed/unpacked), and lifetime token. The allocator will expose a 'pin-for-prefill' hint that prevents eviction of small KV slabs across the prefill->decode boundary for the same request. The kernel ABI is extended with an optional 'inplace-cast' flag. Kernels that implement the flag operate on quantized buffers directly (no intermediate FP32 temp).

Kernel changes: refactor attention kernels to accept quantized input pointers plus scaling parameters. Implement a minimal fast-path for head-sliced QKV where per-head scales are applied in-register rather than via separate passes. For FP8 support, adopt blockwise scale application to avoid per-token branching.

Scheduler: Slimchain keeps a short-lived reservation for the request's KV buffers and tries to route subsequent decode micro-batches onto the same physical slabs. If memory pressure is detected, it will release pinned buffers and trigger a graceful fallback that records telemetry.

Telemetry: add new tags to traces (kernel_path=castless|dequant, pin_hit=true|false) and counters for copy_bytes_saved and additional allocations avoided.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype buffer metadata and allocator pin-for-prefill hint in runtime allocator (Liang)
Week 2: Implement kernel ABI change and a castless attention microkernel (Aisha + Rahul)
Week 3: Integrate Slimchain scheduler decision logic into the request router and add fallback hooks (Liang)
Week 4: Add unit tests, perf harness, and upstream PRs to runtime and kernels repo; run full perf suite on internal CI (perf/stream-7k)
Week 5: Dogfood in staging with a small percentage rollout, collect telemetry, iterate on heuristics
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator pin/unpin semantics and metadata correctness
Microbenchmarks comparing castless vs dequant paths for attention with various head counts and seq lengths
End-to-end integration test: synthetic streaming client that asserts no intermediate copies (validated via copy_bytes_saved metric)
Quality guard: run eval set (eval/regen-1000) to ensure output parity within tolerance
Canary rollout in staging on dedicated small cluster with 5% traffic target, collect perf and error rate
rollout_notes: Initial rollout as opt-in flag runtime.enable_slimchain_castless = true
Monitor copy_bytes_saved and kernel_path counters; have automatic rollback if error-rate or latency regressions > 5%
Expose per-customer toggle for Dedicated customers to opt into castless path due to compatibility concerns
